title: RAG vs long context: is RAG dead?
caption:
Is RAG dead now that models can read huge inputs? Short answer: no. The RAG series finale 👇

→ Long context wins for one long document or a small, fixed set of files
→ RAG wins for large or changing document sets, per-user permissions and cited answers
→ Long context means paying for every token on every question. RAG sends only what's relevant
→ The practical answer is often both: retrieve the right documents, then send whole sections
→ Cache the stable parts of the prompt to cut repeat latency and input token costs (Bedrock prompt caching)

Carry the right chapter to class, not your whole bookshelf.

Save this one 🔖 Which would you pick for your docs: long context, RAG, or both? Tell me in the comments.
Follow @shivanshu_builds for practical AI engineering, one carousel a day.

Sources: Bedrock prompt caching, Bedrock Knowledge Bases retrieval APIs, Bedrock agentic retrieval (docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide)

slides.headline: Is RAG dead? ==Long context vs retrieval.==
slides.sub: When to paste it all in, and when to retrieve.

slides.title: Why not paste everything in?
paragraphs: Models can now read very long inputs, so why not send **all your documents** and skip retrieval?
Think of carrying **every book you own** to class versus bringing the **right chapter**.
slides.callout: Both work for a small shelf. Only one works for a library.

slides.title: Best of ==both==
slides.foot: Bedrock caching cuts ==latency and input token cost.==

slides.title: Agentic retrieval blurs the line
paragraphs: With **agentic retrieval**, a model plans sub-queries and retrieves, then checks if the results are enough.
When it needs more, it can pull **the full content of a document** with `GetDocumentContent`.
slides.callout: It reads a lot, and searches when it needs more.

cta: RAG isn't dead. Long context is just another tool.
Sources: Bedrock prompt caching; Knowledge Bases retrieval APIs; Bedrock agentic retrieval (docs.aws.amazon.com)
